questions: When the board is fully visible, does it hold exactly three pens arranged in a single row?
Are all three pens aligned identically, all pointing the same way, including any pen near the left or right frame edge as it enters or exits?
Do all three pens share identical barrel and cap colors, with no mismatch?
Is every pen fully capped with no exposed writing tip, and are all three pens equal in length?
Does the board advance steadily from left to right at EVERY moment, never halting, freezing, or pausing even briefly (1-3 seconds) at any point in the video?
Do all pens stay fixed in their positions on the board, with no pen shifting, sliding, or moving on its own relative to the board mid-clip?

question_answers.evidence: In frames 8 through 13, when the board is fully visible, there are exactly three pens arranged in a row.

The leftmost pen has its writing tip exposed at the bottom, while the middle and right pens have black caps at the bottom. This indicates a difference in orientation/state (capped vs uncapped) or potentially orientation if the capped pens are tip-down inside the cap.
The leftmost pen appears to have a bare metal/plastic tip at the bottom (dark grey/black point), while the other two have a distinct black cap assembly. They do not look identical.
The leftmost pen clearly shows a bare writing tip (pointy end) at the bottom, whereas the other two pens have black caps covering the ends. This is a 'missing cap' scenario.
The board moves steadily from the left side of the frame to the right side across the sequence without stopping or reversing.
The pens remain fixed in their relative positions on the white board throughout the movement.

parsed.reason: The leftmost pen is uncapped, showing a bare writing tip, while the other two pens are capped with black caps. This violates the nominal condition that all pens must be identical and capped.

description: One pen is missing its cap while the others are capped.
